findings.title: Tampered icejump.properties auto-executes an arbitrary .class
findings.entry_point: The desktop game reads aiLeft and aiRight from the working-directory file icejump.properties (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/ApoIcejumpConstants.java:20,44-53). A second reachable entry is a .class selected through the menu's load action (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpMenu.java:194-197).
findings.sink: ApoIcejumpClassLoader defines bytes read from the selected path with defineClass at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/ApoIcejumpClassLoader.java:60-63 and invokes Class.newInstance at line 36. Instantiation occurs before the instanceof ApoIcejumpAI check at lines 36-38.
findings.data_path: ApoIcejumpPanel.init calls loadProperties (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpPanel.java:224-232); loadPropertiesPlayer treats a non-integer property as a filename and calls loadPlayer (lines 235-249); loadPlayer extracts its path and class name (lines 596-621) and constructs ApoIcejumpClassLoader in the desktop branch (lines 642-648); getAI calls loadClass and newInstance (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/ApoIcejumpClassLoader.java:29-38); loadClassData reads the complete local file (lines 87-98), after which loadClass calls defineClass (lines 54-63).
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker supplies a game directory containing a standalone Evil.class and icejump.properties with aiLeft=Evil.class, then convinces the victim to launch the desktop game with that directory as its working directory. Startup parses Evil.class as an external AI name, loads its bytes, and invokes its zero-argument constructor before checking whether it is an AI. A static initializer or constructor can therefore read or alter the victim's files, start processes, or use the network with the game's OS-account privileges. The same result follows if the victim selects a malicious AI .class using the visible load control.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode must be used; the loader is gated by !ApoConstants.B_APPLET at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpPanel.java:645-648. The attacker must control the working-directory properties/class files or persuade the victim to select the malicious .class.
findings.validation_plan: Compile a public default-package Evil class for the victim's Java version whose static initializer creates a marker file. Put Evil.class and an icejump.properties containing aiLeft=Evil.class in a test launch directory, start the packaged desktop game with that working directory, and confirm that the marker is created during startup. Evil need not extend ApoIcejumpAI because newInstance precedes the type check.

findings.title: Plain-HTTP public-IP lookup permits response spoofing
findings.code_excerpt:
URL url = new URL("http://whatismyip.com/automation/n09230945.asp");
			InputStreamReader in = new InputStreamReader(url.openStream());
findings.entry_point: The first response line supplied by whatismyip.com, a malicious replacement server, or an on-path HTTP attacker enters through getRouterIP at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:64-72.
findings.sink: The unauthenticated response is accepted by URL.openStream at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:68-72 and displayed through drawString at lines 242-253.
findings.data_path: Pressing N in the main menu invokes setNetwork (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpMenu.java:144-145), which calls ApoIcejumpNetwork.start (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpPanel.java:720-724). start creates a thread (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:42-61); run calls getRouterIP and stores its result (lines 163-165); getRouterIP reads and prefixes the HTTP response (lines 64-87); renderNetwork displays myRouterIP (lines 230-245).
findings.attack_scenario: While the victim enters Networkmode, an attacker controlling the network path or DNS intercepts the port-80 request and returns an attacker-selected address such as 203.0.113.66. The game presents that value as the victim's router IP. The attacker gains integrity control over this displayed network configuration value; no credentials, scores, or executable data traverse this particular request, so the impact is limited.
findings.preconditions: The victim must activate Networkmode using the N keyboard shortcut, and outbound HTTP must be possible. The attacker must control the endpoint, DNS resolution, an HTTP proxy, or another position on the network path.
findings.validation_plan: Launch the desktop game with Java HTTP proxy properties pointing to a controlled proxy. Have the proxy return 203.0.113.66 followed by a newline for the hard-coded URL, press N at the menu, and confirm that the network screen displays router IP: 203.0.113.66 without any authentication or warning.

findings.title: Unbounded HTTP response line can exhaust the game heap
findings.entry_point: A malicious whatismyip.com server or on-path HTTP attacker controls the byte stream consumed at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:68-72.
findings.sink: BufferedReader.readLine at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:72 accumulates data until a line terminator or EOF, with no response-size bound.
findings.data_path: The menu's N shortcut reaches ApoIcejumpPanel.setNetwork (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpMenu.java:144-145; _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpPanel.java:720-724). ApoIcejumpNetwork.start creates a new lookup thread (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:42-61); run calls getRouterIP (lines 163-165), which passes the attacker-controlled stream directly to readLine (lines 64-72).
findings.attack_scenario: After the victim enters Networkmode, the attacker answers the HTTP request with a continuous, very large sequence of bytes containing no CR or LF. readLine continues growing its in-memory line buffer until the lookup thread or JVM encounters OutOfMemoryError, denying or destabilizing the game process.
findings.preconditions: The victim must enter Networkmode and the attacker must control the HTTP response path. The response connection must remain open while streaming a line large enough to approach the JVM heap limit.
findings.validation_plan: Run the packaged game with a small test heap such as -Xmx64m and a controlled HTTP proxy. Configure the proxy to stream bytes indefinitely without a newline for the hard-coded URL, press N, and observe an OutOfMemoryError in the lookup thread, process termination on an exit-on-OOM JVM, or loss of responsiveness. Repeat with a bounded newline-terminated response as the control case.

notes: The source root contains only 76 decompiled Java files under _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded; no build files, resources, or runnable JAR were available for dynamic confirmation. Four AI classes imported at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpMenu.java:13-16 are absent, so their unavailable bytecode was not audited. No ObjectInputStream, MessageDigest/MD5, JNI load, corpus save/replay suffix, highscore endpoint, or level-sharing endpoint appears in the available source. ApoIcejumpPanel.loadLevel and saveLevel are empty (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/game/ApoIcejumpPanel.java:820-827). The plain-HTTP APPLET_LEVEL string at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/apoIcejump/ApoIcejumpComponent.java:26 and the URL-capable abstract ApoIO methods at _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/org/apogames/ApoIO.java:136-244 have no game call site or concrete ApoIO subclass, so they are theoretical library surface rather than reachable findings. Likewise, org.apogames.help.ApoClassLoader can construct a URLClassLoader and instantiate a class (_from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:62-75), but the variant never calls getMyClass or constructs that loader; it was therefore not reported separately.
